purpose: Operate the recurring side of a CCTV-and-cloud-recording business site by site: keep every camera verifiably recording, manage cloud storage and the promised retention window, retrieve incident footage with verified authority and evidence integrity, hold each site inside its jurisdiction's privacy, consent and signage obligation classes, control and audit who views footage, and run proof-of-value reporting, honest renewals, saves and clean offboarding that protect per-site recurring revenue.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is an own-build local installer-operator running its own cloud-video subscription under its own brand, not an agent or franchisee of a major security company

each site arrives in operations already surveyed, installed, segmented and commissioned by the design-and-installation practice; operations maintains and runs what was built rather than redesigning it

storage costs, churn behavior and service economics are treated as mechanisms or qualitative bands verified against the operator's own vendor bills, account records and site history, never as asserted market figures

surveillance is operated only for lawful, disclosed purposes - deterrence, detection and evidence for the property owner - and the recorded footage is handled as the owner's sensitive data, not the operator's asset

video privacy, audio-recording consent, signage and disclosure rules vary sharply by jurisdiction, so every site carries a verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction flag that operations must keep current
exclusions: productizing and pricing the offer: subscription tier design, segment targeting, VSaaS-platform-versus-own-stack selection economics, hardware-versus-subscription margin architecture and ethical new-deal selling - the surveillance offer design and pricing KB owns these

designing and building the system: site survey and coverage design, camera selection and placement, edge/cloud/hybrid recording architecture and its design-time bandwidth and storage sizing math, initial network segmentation and hardening, cabling and commissioning tests - the camera system design and installation KB owns these; this KB maintains what that one hands over

covert or unlawful monitoring in any form: hidden cameras, undisclosed audio capture, pointing coverage into spaces the owner has no right to record, or helping any party watch people without disclosure - such requests are declined and documented, never operated

asserting jurisdiction-specific legal requirements, retention statutes, storage prices or churn rates as fact - obligations are named as classes with a verify-locally flag and quantities are described as mechanisms verified against the operator's own records

personalized legal advice on privacy, employment or evidence matters - the operator names the obligation class, flags local verification and directs the customer to qualified local counsel for specifics

competency_questions.question: What exactly does the monthly subscription obligate the operator to keep doing at a site, and where does lawful operation of the service end?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_CHARTER enumerates the recurring obligations the subscription promises and LAWFUL_USE_BOUNDARY states the disclosed-purpose limits and the decline rule for covert or out-of-right monitoring requests

competency_questions.question: Which privacy, consent and signage obligation classes apply at a given site, and how are they kept current and visibly satisfied?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JURISDICTION_PRIVACY_REGISTER names the obligation classes per site with a verify-locally flag and review date, and CONSENT_AND_SIGNAGE_OPS translates them into operated signage, audio posture and consent artifacts

competency_questions.question: How is a site's retention schedule set, enforced by automation, and lawfully excepted when footage must outlive its window?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_POLICY_ENGINE defines the per-camera-group retention windows, the purge automation that enforces them and their contract linkage, and LEGAL_HOLD_AND_EXPORT_INTEGRITY defines the hold that suspends purging

competency_questions.question: Who may view or export footage at each site, how is that access granted and revoked, and how does the operator prove afterward who watched what?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCESS_CONTROL_MODEL specifies the least-privilege role matrix, credential rules and revocation events, and VIEW_AUDIT_TRAIL specifies the view/export log, its review cadence and the anomaly escalation path

competency_questions.question: How does the operator detect a dying or silently dead camera before the customer needs its footage, and what happens when the alert fires?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAMERA_HEALTH_MONITORING lists the health signals including recording-gap detection and image-quality degradation, and ALERT_TRIAGE_RUNBOOK gives the severity classes, remote-first fix ladder and truck-roll decision rule

competency_questions.question: What mechanisms drive a site's cloud storage consumption and cost, and how is drift between promised plan and actual usage caught and resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STORAGE_CAPACITY_OPS explains consumption as the product of camera count, resolution/bitrate settings, recording mode and retention window, and defines the reconciliation loop that surfaces drift with its cause

competency_questions.question: How is an incident-footage request executed end to end so the export is fast, authorized and usable as evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCIDENT_RETRIEVAL_WORKFLOW covers intake, time-window narrowing, clip assembly and logged delivery, and LEGAL_HOLD_AND_EXPORT_INTEGRITY covers original-format export, integrity markers and the no-editing rule

competency_questions.question: What does the operator do when someone other than the account owner - police, an insurer, an employee, a neighbor - asks for footage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THIRD_PARTY_REQUEST_HANDLING requires verified requester authority plus owner authorization or a valid legal instrument before any release, names the request classes, and logs every disclosure decision

competency_questions.question: How does the fleet stay patched, credentialed and isolated over years of operation rather than only on install day?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRMWARE_AND_VULN_HYGIENE defines the patch cadence, vulnerability watch, staged rollout, credential hygiene and the isolation spot-check performed on service visits

competency_questions.question: How does the operator prove every month that the subscription is worth paying, and how do service-plan tiers shape what is owed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_PLAN_TIERS_OPS maps each tier to its operated response and reporting classes, and PROOF_OF_VALUE_REPORTING defines the periodic report of uptime, fixes and retrievals that includes failures honestly

competency_questions.question: What actually drives churn on camera subscriptions, which drivers can operations remove, and how are at-risk accounts saved ethically?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHURN_DRIVER_MAP names the driver classes and separates ops-removable from structural ones, and SAVE_AND_WINBACK_PLAYS gives root-cause-first save moves that never rely on hidden re-lock terms

competency_questions.question: What do an honest renewal and a clean cancellation look like for a camera subscription?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_RENEWAL_PRACTICE requires plain advance notice, disclosed term changes and right-sizing on actual usage, and OFFBOARDING_AND_DATA_DISPOSITION requires the final export offer, credential revocation and documented data disposition

competency_questions.question: How does the operation learn from failed retrievals, alert noise, audit findings and churn instead of repeating them?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OPS_REVIEW_AND_IMPROVEMENT runs postmortems and a recurring review that retunes alerting, refreshes the privacy register and feeds systemic findings back to the offer and design practices through the documented handoff

glossary.definition: A span of time for which a camera that should have been recording produced no stored footage - caused by outage, misconfiguration, storage failure or tampering - detectable by comparing expected timeline coverage against stored segments; the single most dangerous silent failure in a cloud video service.

The per-site, per-camera-group period for which recorded footage is kept before automatic deletion; it is a contractual promise and a privacy commitment at once, set from the owner's stated need and the jurisdiction's obligation classes, and enforced by purge automation.
The scheduled deletion of footage that has aged past its retention window; correct purge proves the privacy promise is real, and its only lawful exception is an active legal hold.

A suspension of auto-purge for identified footage when litigation, an investigation or a preservation request makes deletion improper; the hold is scoped, dated, logged and released explicitly rather than left open forever.

An incident clip delivered in original recorded format with its timestamps, source-camera identity and an integrity marker such as a cryptographic hash, plus a log of who exported it when - so the recipient can rely on it not having been edited.

An access grant that gives a named person only the cameras, functions and time ranges their duty requires - a shift manager sees the sales floor live but cannot export, while the owner holds export rights - instead of one shared all-camera login.

The tamper-resistant log of every footage view, search and export - who, which camera, which time range, when - reviewed on a cadence so misuse of surveillance against staff or customers is detectable and demonstrable.

The posted notices that tell people entering a monitored space that recording is in progress, worded and placed to satisfy the site's jurisdictional obligation class; operations re-verifies signage on service visits because remodels and repaints quietly remove it.

Dispatching a technician to the site physically; the most expensive move in recurring service economics, justified only after the remote fix ladder is exhausted or when hardware, cabling or safety requires hands on site.

A retention move made to an account signalling cancellation - fixing the root grievance, right-sizing the plan, or pausing service - which is legitimate only when its terms are stated plainly and it never smuggles in a hidden term extension.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cloud_video_operations_and_privacy_compliance work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix what the monthly subscription actually obligates the operator to keep doing at each site, in writing, before any of it is operated: continuous recording per the configured schedule, camera-health monitoring with stated detection and response classes, storage and retention management to the promised window, incident retrieval help, viewer access administration and periodic service reporting. The charter converts the sold offer into an operations contract - per site, per tier - so every downstream runbook has a definition of done and the customer's expectations match what the crew actually does. It also states what the subscription does not include, so scope creep is negotiated instead of silently absorbed.

excluded: designing or pricing the tiers themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the sold offer's obligations change or dispute patterns reveal a missing charter clause

pros.claim: A written obligation charter stops the recurring service from being redefined by whoever complains loudest
pros.example: a restaurant owner demanding free after-hours camera relocation is shown the charter line that relocations are billable design changes

cons.claim: A rigid charter can read as small print and sour a relationship if it is quoted instead of served
cons.example: citing the not-included list to a loyal site whose one small favor request would have cost ten minutes

failure_modes: operating from the salesperson's verbal promises so every crew member serves a different contract
leaving the not-included list unwritten and eating unbounded free work until margins vanish
acceptance_tests: every active site has a charter listing its obligations, tier, retention window, reporting cadence and not-included items, and the operations crew works from it rather than from memory
revisit_triggers: the offer practice changes a tier's promises
recurring disputes show the charter is silent on a class of request

nodes.definition: Enforce, throughout the life of the subscription, the boundary the business sold under: surveillance exists for deterrence, detection and evidence for the property owner, operated openly in spaces the owner has the right to record. Operations is where this boundary gets tested - a customer asks mid-contract to aim a camera into a neighbor's lot, to add a hidden camera in a break area, to switch on audio without consent posture, or to use footage to settle a personal score - and the rule is a documented decline with the reason, the jurisdictional flag and the alternative that stays lawful. The boundary applies to the operator's own staff too: support technicians view footage only for a ticketed service reason.

included: decline rule for covert or out-of-right requests
purpose limitation on all viewing including staff
excluded: drafting the customer's internal workplace policies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a declined-request dispute, a staff-viewing incident, or a legal change in permissible surveillance scope

pros.claim: A hard, documented decline rule protects the operator's license to exist when a customer's request would create liability for both parties
pros.example: refusing a bar owner's request to point a camera at the rival's entrance across the street, with the refusal and reason logged

cons.claim: Declining a paying customer's request can cost the account even when the refusal is correct
cons.example: a site cancels after being told a concealed office camera aimed at one employee's desk will not be installed or supported

failure_modes: quietly accommodating one covert request and normalizing unlawful operation across the book
support staff browsing customer footage without a ticketed reason because nothing forbids it
acceptance_tests: every covert, out-of-right or undisclosed-audio request is declined in writing with the reason and a lawful alternative offered, and staff viewing is tied to service tickets
revisit_triggers: a request pattern emerges the boundary text does not clearly cover
a jurisdiction's definition of permissible workplace surveillance changes

nodes.definition: Maintain a per-site register of the privacy obligation classes that govern its operation: video-surveillance disclosure rules, audio-recording consent regimes (one-party, all-party or prohibition classes), workplace-monitoring notice duties, data-protection classes that may treat footage as personal data with access and deletion rights, and any sector overlays such as premises that serve minors or medical clients. The register never asserts the specific legal text - it names the class, records what the site currently does about it, carries a verify-current-rules-in-your-jurisdiction flag with the date last checked, and drives the retention, signage and disclosure settings downstream. It is operations' single answer to 'what are we obliged to do here'.

included: obligation classes per site with last-verified date
verify-locally flag as a standing field
linkage to retention, signage and disclosure settings
excluded: asserting specific statutes or thresholds as fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any signal that a listed obligation class changed or that a site's circumstances moved it into a new class

pros.claim: A living register turns vague legal anxiety into a checkable per-site artifact that survives staff turnover
pros.example: a new technician sees at a glance that a dental-office site runs audio-off with patient-area signage because of its consent and sector classes

cons.claim: A register can create false comfort if its verify dates go stale while rules move
cons.example: a site operated for two years on an entry checked once at install, missing a new employee-notice duty

failure_modes: copying one site's register to another jurisdiction without re-verification
recording obligation classes but never wiring them to actual retention and signage settings
acceptance_tests: every site's register names its obligation classes, the operated response to each, a verify-locally flag and a last-verified date within the review cadence
revisit_triggers: a legal change notice, customer counsel input or industry alert touches a listed class
a site changes use, tenancy or jurisdiction
the periodic register review date arrives

nodes.definition: Set and enforce each site's retention schedule as a first-class design decision, not a storage default: per camera group, choose the window from the owner's stated evidence need (how late incidents are typically discovered), the jurisdiction's obligation classes, and the storage economics of the plan - then write it into the contract and configure auto-purge to execute it exactly. The engine covers differentiated windows (a cash-office camera may warrant a longer window than a dining room), the documentation that proves footage really is deleted on schedule, and the single sanctioned exception path of a legal hold. Retention is simultaneously a promise to the customer, a privacy commitment to the people recorded, and the biggest lever on cloud cost - which is why it is decided deliberately.

included: purge automation matching the documented schedule
excluded: design-time storage sizing math for new installs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a purge failure, an out-of-window incident, or a register change that moves a site's permissible or required window

pros.claim: Deliberate per-group retention matches evidence value to cost instead of paying to keep everything forever
pros.example: a contractor's yard keeps a long window on the gate camera where thefts surface late, and a short one on the office corridor

cons.claim: Every retention window will someday be one day shorter than an incident needed, and the customer will remember only that
cons.example: a slip-and-fall claim arriving just after the promised window purged the relevant week

failure_modes: running platform default retention that neither matches the contract nor the register
purge automation silently failing so footage outlives its promise and the privacy commitment is false
acceptance_tests: each camera group's configured retention equals its documented and contracted window, purge execution is evidenced, and the only override on record is a scoped legal hold
revisit_triggers: an incident falls outside the window and triggers a retention review
the privacy register changes an obligation class touching retention
storage reconciliation shows the window is mispriced for the plan

nodes.definition: Operate the visible half of privacy compliance for the life of each site: recording-in-progress signage present, legible and placed where people enter monitored space; the audio posture (audio disabled by default, enabled only where the register's consent class permits and the owner has documented the consent basis); and the consent artifacts the site relies on, such as employee-notice acknowledgments the owner collected. Signage decays in the real world - remodels remove it, new entrances open unposted, sun bleaches it - so every service visit includes a signage-and-posture check with photo evidence, and any change to camera coverage triggers a re-check. This node keeps the disclosure that makes the surveillance lawful true in practice, not just in the file.

included: signage presence and placement upkeep with photo evidence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a signage gap found on visit, an audio-posture drift, or a consent-class change in the register

pros.claim: Routine photo-evidenced signage checks turn an invisible legal exposure into a cheap recurring checklist item
pros.example: a technician's visit photo shows the back-entrance sign vanished during repainting, fixed the same day for the cost of a sign

cons.claim: Signage upkeep is easy to dismiss as trivia until the one unposted entrance becomes the incident location
cons.example: footage from a new side door gets challenged because no notice was posted there for six months

failure_modes: enabling audio on a camera swap because the new model ships with it on, breaching the site's consent class
treating signage as install-day scenery that no one ever re-verifies
acceptance_tests: each site's latest service visit includes dated signage photos, a confirmed audio posture matching the register, and any coverage change carries its re-check record
revisit_triggers: a remodel, tenancy change or new entrance at a site
the register changes the site's consent or notice class

nodes.definition: Administer who can see and export footage at every site on a least-privilege basis: named individual accounts (never shared logins), roles scoped to the cameras and functions a duty requires, export rights reserved to the owner or a designated few, multi-factor authentication on every account, and the operator's own support access limited, ticketed and time-bounded. The model includes the lifecycle events that actually break access control in small businesses - an employee leaves, a manager changes role, the business is sold - each mapped to a same-week revocation or re-scope, and a periodic access recertification where the owner confirms every account still belongs to someone who should have it. Access administration is the difference between a surveillance service and a voyeurism liability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an access misuse event, a recertification finding, or platform changes to role and MFA capabilities

pros.claim: Named, scoped accounts make every view attributable and shrink the blast radius of any single compromised credential
pros.example: when a retail site's assistant manager quits, one account is revoked in minutes instead of rotating a shared password nobody remembers everywhere

cons.claim: Owners experience per-person accounts and MFA as friction and lobby for one shared login on the office tablet
cons.example: a motel owner taping the shared password to the front desk monitor because individual logins felt slow at shift change

failure_modes: terminated staff retaining viewer access for months because no revocation event exists
the operator's own technicians holding standing admin access to every customer's footage
acceptance_tests: every account at every site maps to a named current person with a scoped role and MFA, support access is ticket-bound, and the latest recertification is within its cadence
revisit_triggers: an audit anomaly or a compromised-credential event
a site reports staff turnover or an ownership change

nodes.definition: Keep and actually use the audit trail of footage access: every view, search, export and share captured with who, which camera, which time range and when; the log protected from the people it audits; a review cadence proportionate to site sensitivity; and an anomaly path for patterns that suggest misuse - repeated scrubbing of a staff-only area with no incident ticket, exports at odd hours, one viewer consuming footage of one person. Findings route to the site owner (it is their duty to manage their staff's use) and, where the operator's own staff appear, to the operator's management. The audit trail is what lets an honest operator prove a negative - that footage was not browsed, leaked or misused - which is exactly what an upset employee, a data-protection inquiry or a court will ask.

included: escalation to owner or operator management
excluded: granting and revoking the access itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an anomaly disposition, a misuse complaint, or a change in the platform's audit-event coverage

pros.claim: A reviewed audit trail converts 'trust us' into demonstrable accountability for the most sensitive thing the service holds
pros.example: answering an employee's misuse complaint with the log showing her workstation camera was viewed only twice, both under incident tickets she knew about

cons.claim: An unreviewed log is dead weight that documents misuse without ever surfacing it
cons.example: months of nightly exports by one account discovered only when the aggrieved party's lawyer asked for the log

failure_modes: logging views but never reviewing them so anomalies age into scandals
letting site admins edit or disable the very log that audits them
acceptance_tests: the trail captures view, search and export events for every site, the last review is within cadence, and each anomaly on record shows a disposition
revisit_triggers: an anomaly finding or misuse complaint
a platform change alters what events are logged or how long log history is kept

nodes.definition: Watch the deployed fleet so a camera failure is an operations event, not a customer discovery: online/offline state, recording-gap detection that compares expected timeline coverage against stored segments (the check that catches the camera that is 'up' but writing nothing), image-quality degradation (lens dirt, spider webs across IR at night, focus drift, glare after a fixture change), storage-write errors, clock drift that corrupts timestamp evidence, and firmware state. Health is scored per camera and rolled up per site, alerts route by severity into triage, and the health history feeds proof-of-value reporting. The economics are blunt: the subscription's core promise is 'the footage will be there', and this node is the only thing that makes that promise true between install day and the incident.

included: offline, recording-gap, image-quality, storage and clock signals
per-camera health score and site rollup

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a missed failure class, a retrieval that exposed an undetected gap, or new health telemetry becoming available

pros.claim: Recording-gap detection catches the deadliest failure class - cameras that look alive but store nothing
pros.example: a corrupted SD-and-cloud sync left a laundromat's till camera streaming live yet writing no history, caught by the coverage check in a day

cons.claim: Health monitoring at fleet scale generates noise that can bury the one alert that matters
cons.example: a hundred nightly short-offline blips from one flaky ISP drowning the single camera that went permanently dark

failure_modes: monitoring only up/down state and missing recording gaps and image degradation
silencing a noisy site instead of fixing its underlying connectivity
acceptance_tests: every camera in the book reports health on the monitoring cadence, recording-gap checks run against expected coverage, and each alert reaches triage with severity and site context
revisit_triggers: an incident retrieval fails on a gap the monitoring missed
alert-noise review shows real failures were buried
a platform or firmware change alters the health signals available

nodes.definition: Turn health alerts into resolved cameras at sane cost: classify severity (a dead camera covering the safe outranks a hazy parking-lot view), then walk the remote-first ladder - reboot the camera, power-cycle the PoE port, re-provision the stream, check the site's internet - before spending a truck roll, and when hands on site are required, batch the visit with due signage checks and other low-severity fixes at that site. The runbook sets who communicates what to the customer and when: a camera the customer relies on being down is their risk exposure, so notification at detection with an honest fix expectation set by the plan tier's response class, not by optimism. Every closed alert records cause and fix so recurring offenders surface in the ops review.

included: remote-first fix ladder and truck-roll rule
excluded: warranty and hardware replacement commercial terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: triage outcome data showing the ladder, severity classes or truck-roll rule are mistuned

pros.claim: The remote-first ladder resolves most alerts without the visit cost that erodes subscription margin
pros.example: a frozen stream at a taqueria fixed by a remote PoE power-cycle during the morning check instead of an afternoon drive across town

cons.claim: Remote-first can waste days retrying a camera whose water-damaged housing only a visit would reveal
cons.example: three remote re-provisions of a yard camera that had rain in its junction box since the storm

failure_modes: treating all alerts equally so the safe camera waits behind cosmetic fixes
closing alerts without cause records, leaving chronic failures invisible
acceptance_tests: each alert on record shows severity, the ladder steps attempted, the tier-classed response met or an escalation note, customer notification where due, and a cause-and-fix entry
revisit_triggers: the ops review finds chronic repeat alerts or ladder steps that never succeed
a tier's response class changes

nodes.definition: Manage each site's cloud storage consumption as the mechanism it is: consumption is driven by camera count, resolution and bitrate settings, recording mode (continuous versus motion-event), scene activity and the retention window, and the operator's cloud bill moves with all five. Operations reconciles actual consumption against what the plan assumed on a cadence, names the cause of any drift - a camera bumped to a higher bitrate during a service swap, a motion-event site whose new neighbor's floodlight triggers all night, retention extended after an incident and never reverted - and resolves it on the correct side: retune settings where the promise is unaffected, or take a plan-fit conversation to the customer where their real usage outgrew what they bought. What this node never does is quietly shorten a promised retention window to make a bill smaller.

excluded: design-time bandwidth and storage sizing for new installs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: vendor pricing changes, reconciliation results, or a quality regression traced to consumption tuning

pros.claim: Cadenced reconciliation catches margin leaks while they are settings problems instead of year-end surprises
pros.example: one site's cloud usage doubling after a technician left a swapped camera on its factory maximum bitrate, caught the next cycle

cons.claim: Aggressive consumption tuning can degrade the footage quality the whole service exists to provide
cons.example: a bitrate cut that saved storage but made the license plates at the gate unreadable at night

failure_modes: eating storage-cost drift silently until the account is unprofitable and the renewal becomes a shock reprice
cutting retention or quality below the contracted promise to control the bill
acceptance_tests: each reconciliation cycle records per-site consumption against plan assumptions, names the cause of any material drift, and shows the resolution chosen without any silent reduction of promised retention or evidentiary quality
revisit_triggers: the cloud vendor changes its pricing or metering model
a site's usage pattern shifts materially
a quality complaint follows a settings retune

nodes.definition: Keep the fleet's security posture alive for years after the installer's hardening: watch vulnerability disclosures for the camera models and recorder platforms actually deployed in the book, patch on a cadence with staged rollouts (a pilot group first, the fleet after the pilot survives), maintain credential hygiene (no default passwords ever reappear via replacements or resets, service credentials rotated on staff departure), keep certificates current, and spot-check on every service visit that the camera network is still isolated the way the installation practice built it - because a customer's new IT helper un-VLANs things. Cameras are among the most hijacked devices on the internet; an operator whose fleet joins a botnet or leaks streams loses the book and deserves to. This node maintains the wall; building it belonged to the design-and-installation practice.

included: vulnerability watch and staged patch cadence
credential and certificate hygiene over time
excluded: initial network segmentation and hardening design

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an advisory affecting deployed hardware, a compromise event in the field, or a failed staged rollout

pros.claim: Staged rollouts convert vendor firmware risk into a small pilot problem instead of a fleet outage
pros.example: a bad vendor release that broke night mode was caught on five pilot cameras instead of every site in the book overnight

cons.claim: Patch discipline consumes recurring hours the subscription price must actually carry
cons.example: a month with three vendor advisories eating the margin of the smallest sites' monitoring time

failure_modes: a replacement camera going in with default credentials because swaps bypass the hardening checklist
deferring a disclosed remote-exploit patch until customer streams appear where they should never be
acceptance_tests: the deployed-model list maps to watched advisories, patch state per camera is current within the cadence or has a dated exception, no default credentials exist in the fleet, and the latest visit spot-checks confirm isolation
revisit_triggers: a vulnerability disclosure touching deployed models
an isolation spot-check failure
a pilot-group patch failure

nodes.definition: Run the workflow the customer is really paying for: something happened, and footage must be found, clipped and delivered while it matters. Intake captures who is asking, what happened, where and in what time band; authority is confirmed against the access model; the search narrows by camera and window using motion and event indexes rather than scrubbing hours linearly; the clip is assembled with adjacent context (the minutes before a fall often matter more than the fall); and delivery is logged with recipient, purpose and timestamp. The workflow carries a response expectation set by the plan tier, an escalation for law-enforcement-urgency cases, and a defined answer for the request that cannot be satisfied - footage outside retention, a camera that was down - delivered honestly with what the operator will change, because a fumbled 'no' here is the single strongest churn event in the vertical.

included: intake, authority check, indexed search, clip assembly, logged delivery

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retrieval outcome records, a failed or late retrieval postmortem, or new platform search capabilities

pros.claim: A practiced retrieval pipeline delivers the moment of proven value that anchors every renewal after it
pros.example: a c-store owner receiving the clean till-skim clip the same afternoon he reported the drawer discrepancy

cons.claim: Retrieval work arrives unscheduled and clustered, and a busy week can wreck the response promise
cons.example: one storm weekend producing break-in requests from four sites at once for a one-person ops bench

failure_modes: delivering fast but unauthorized - handing footage to a caller nobody verified
linear scrubbing burning hours the tier's economics never priced
acceptance_tests: every retrieval on record shows intake, an authority check, the search method, delivery logged with recipient and purpose, and response inside the tier class or an escalation note; unsatisfiable requests show the honest explanation given
revisit_triggers: a retrieval misses its response class or fails on a gap
request volume or pattern shifts materially across the book

nodes.definition: Adjudicate footage requests that do not come from the account owner, because they will come: police canvassing after a neighborhood incident, an insurer investigating a claim, an employee who believes footage exonerates them, a neighbor wanting proof of a fence dispute, a landlord curious about a tenant. The rule structure: the footage is the owner's data; release requires verified requester identity and authority plus the owner's documented authorization, or a legal instrument of the class that compels production - and which instruments compel what varies by jurisdiction, so the register's verify-locally flag applies to every contested case. Data-protection classes in some jurisdictions give recorded individuals their own access-request rights, which are logged and routed with the same discipline. Every disclosure decision - grant, decline or refer to counsel - is logged with its basis, and urgency never substitutes for authority.

included: request classes and the authority-plus-authorization rule
excluded: giving legal opinions on a specific instrument's validity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a disputed disclosure outcome or a change in the jurisdiction's compelled-production or data-subject-rights classes

pros.claim: A fixed adjudication rule protects the operator from becoming the person who leaked a customer's footage under social pressure
pros.example: a polite decline-and-refer to an insurance investigator phoning for parking-lot footage without the owner's sign-off, logged the same hour

cons.claim: Strict verification can slow cooperation in cases where fast footage genuinely serves public safety
cons.example: a canvassing officer waiting for the owner's callback authorization while a suspect vehicle description goes stale

failure_modes: releasing footage on a convincing phone call because refusing felt rude
failing to log a disclosure and having no answer when the owner asks who saw their footage
acceptance_tests: every third-party request on record shows requester identity and authority verification, owner authorization or the compelling instrument's class, the decision with its basis, and the verify-locally flag consulted for contested classes
revisit_triggers: a contested disclosure or refusal
the register updates a jurisdiction's disclosure or data-subject-rights class

nodes.definition: Handle the two moments when footage stops being ordinary data and becomes evidence. First, the legal hold: when a preservation letter, litigation notice or investigation makes deletion improper, auto-purge is suspended for the identified cameras and windows - scoped, dated, logged, and released explicitly when the matter closes, never left as an open-ended exception that quietly defeats the retention promise. Second, export integrity: evidence-bound clips leave in original recorded format with native timestamps and source-camera identity, carry an integrity marker such as a cryptographic hash recorded at export, and are never trimmed for flattery, re-encoded into ambiguity or annotated in ways that alter content; the export log ties each artifact to who produced it and when. The operator's role is faithful custodian of what the cameras saw - enhancement and interpretation belong to the parties and their experts.

included: scoped hold placement, logging and release
excluded: opining on litigation strategy or instrument validity

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a hold event, a challenged export, or platform changes to export formats and integrity features

pros.claim: Disciplined holds and hash-marked exports make the operator's footage dependable when it matters most
pros.example: an injury claim two years on, answered by the hold record and a hash-verifiable clip instead of a shrug about purged data

cons.claim: Holds that never get released accumulate into a shadow archive that betrays the retention promise
cons.example: a site carrying three years of held footage for a claim that settled quietly the first winter

failure_modes: auto-purge deleting footage after a preservation notice arrived but was never actioned
delivering a convenience-trimmed re-encode that a competent opposing expert dismantles
acceptance_tests: every hold on record is scoped to cameras and windows with placement and release dates, purge suspension is verified effective, and every evidence-bound export shows original format, integrity marker and its export-log entry
revisit_triggers: a hold is placed, challenged or overdue for release review
an export's integrity is questioned by a recipient

nodes.definition: Operate the service-plan ladder the offer practice designed, and keep delivery matched to what each tier's subscribers actually bought: which response class an alert gets, what the reporting cadence is, whether after-hours retrieval help is included, what hardware-swap terms apply. Operations owns the honest mechanics of tiering - a premium site must receive premium handling visibly, a basic site must never be silently upgraded into unpriced work that trains the customer to expect it, and when a site's usage repeatedly exceeds its tier (frequent retrievals, chronic after-hours calls), the answer is a documented plan-fit conversation, not resentful free service or silent degradation. Tier delivery data - what each class of site actually costs to serve - flows back to the offer practice as the mechanism evidence behind future pricing.

included: cost-to-serve evidence back to the offer practice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tier redefinition by the offer practice or cost-to-serve data contradicting a tier's assumptions

pros.claim: Visible tier differentiation makes the upgrade conversation honest: the customer buys handling they can see exists
pros.example: a pawn shop on the top tier watching its dead camera get same-day attention its neighbor's basic plan did not promise

cons.claim: Tier discipline can feel petty at the margin and be worked around by soft-hearted technicians
cons.example: a crew habitually giving a friendly basic-tier cafe premium response until its owner shops the formal upgrade quote around in disbelief

failure_modes: delivering one undifferentiated service level so upper tiers are pure overcharge
letting chronic over-usage ride unaddressed until the account is deeply unprofitable
acceptance_tests: service records per site match the tier's promised response and reporting classes, and sustained mismatches show a dated plan-fit conversation
revisit_triggers: the offer practice revises tier definitions
cost-to-serve evidence shows a tier is structurally mispriced

nodes.definition: Publish, on the cadence each tier promises, the report that makes the invisible subscription visible: camera uptime and health events with what was fixed and how fast, recording-coverage confirmation, retrievals performed and their outcomes, storage and retention status, and any signage or access changes made. The report includes failures honestly - the camera that was down two days, the retrieval that missed its window - together with cause and corrective action, because a report that only ever says 'all fine' reads as wallpaper and dies unread, while an honest one builds the credibility the renewal will stand on. For a service whose best months are the ones where nothing happened, this report is the recurring answer to 'what am I paying for' - it is deterrence, coverage assurance and maintenance made legible.

included: uptime, fixes, retrievals, retention and access-change reporting
honest failure inclusion with corrective action
excluded: churn analysis built on top of the reports

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: renewal feedback on report usefulness or a report-versus-records discrepancy

pros.claim: A concrete monthly artifact converts silent uptime into remembered value at renewal time
pros.example: a yard owner flipping through twelve reports showing four caught camera failures and one theft clip before signing renewal without a discount demand

cons.claim: Reporting effort scales with the book and can decay into templated noise nobody reads
cons.example: identical auto-generated pages for every site until a customer finds his offline week described as normal operation

failure_modes: hiding failures and having the customer discover one independently, poisoning trust worse than the failure did
reporting platform vanity numbers instead of the events the owner actually cares about
acceptance_tests: each site's latest report matches its tier cadence, reconciles with health and retrieval records including failures, and states corrective actions taken
revisit_triggers: renewal conversations show the report is unread or unpersuasive
a discrepancy between a report and the underlying records surfaces

nodes.definition: Maintain the operator's map of why camera subscriptions actually die, separated into drivers operations can remove and drivers it can only see coming. Ops-removable: the silent dead camera discovered at incident time (the trust-destroying event), failed or fumbled retrievals, chronic unaddressed alerts, invisible value (no reporting), and billing surprises from unmanaged storage drift. Structural: the business closes or moves, ownership changes and the new owner has a cousin in the trade, a national platform undercuts on price, or the customer decides a one-time DIY kit is enough after years without incident. Each churn event in the book gets a recorded root cause against this taxonomy, at-risk signals (declining logins, unpaid invoices, unanswered reports, a for-sale listing) get watched, and the map's shifting mix is the operator's earliest strategic instrument - a rising ops-removable share is self-inflicted damage with a fix, a rising structural share is market information for the offer practice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: each churn event's root cause, exit-interview evidence, or a shift in the driver mix across a review period

pros.claim: Root-caused churn separates fixable operational failure from market weather, so effort lands where it works
pros.example: a quarter's exits splitting into two dead-camera discoveries worth fixing forever and one unpreventable business closure

cons.claim: Small-book churn data is lumpy, and a single bad quarter can be misread as a trend
cons.example: three closures on the same declining retail strip masquerading as a service-quality problem

failure_modes: recording churn as 'price' because that is what departing customers politely say
watching no at-risk signals so every cancellation arrives as a surprise
acceptance_tests: every churn event in the period carries a root cause against the taxonomy, and the at-risk watchlist shows the signals monitored per account
revisit_triggers: the driver mix shifts materially between reviews
a save or exit interview contradicts the recorded root cause

nodes.definition: Run renewals the way the business wants to be known: plain advance notice before any term renews, every change in price or terms stated explicitly rather than slipped into an auto-renewal, no evergreen traps engineered to catch the inattentive, and a right-sizing review that uses the year's actual service record - health events, retrievals, storage consumption - to confirm the site is on the plan that fits, including recommending a cheaper tier when the usage says so. The renewal conversation is built on the proof-of-value reports already delivered, so it is a summary of known facts rather than a sales ambush. Cancellation is honored without obstruction: an operator whose churn defense is contract handcuffs has already lost the book, because in a small-business community the exit experience is marketing to every neighbor.

included: plain advance notice and disclosed changes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a notice dispute, consumer-protection guidance on auto-renewal classes changing, or right-sizing outcomes at scale

pros.claim: Renewals built on delivered evidence and honest terms compound into the referral reputation that fills the pipeline
pros.example: a restaurant owner renewing over coffee in five minutes and sending the operator to her brother's warehouse the same week

cons.claim: Transparent renewals surrender the passive revenue that silent auto-renewal and forgotten upcharges harvest
cons.example: proactively downgrading an over-tiered quiet site and watching its invoice shrink by the operator's own recommendation

failure_modes: letting terms auto-renew changed and unannounced, then defending it as 'in the contract' to a furious customer
skipping right-sizing so mis-tiered accounts accumulate quiet resentment until they leave at once
acceptance_tests: every renewal on record shows dated advance notice, explicit statement of any change, a usage-based fit review, and any cancellation processed without obstruction steps
revisit_triggers: a renewal dispute over notice or terms
right-sizing recommendations repeatedly contradicting tier definitions

nodes.definition: Respond to cancellation signals with moves that fix causes instead of hiding them: when an account wobbles, first pull its root cause from the churn map - if the grievance is operational (a dead camera, a failed retrieval, a billing surprise), the save is the fix plus what changed so it cannot recur; if the mismatch is economic, the save is a right-sized or paused plan stated plainly; if the driver is structural (closure, sale), the play is a dignified exit that plants a winback seed - the new owner of the premises inherits a documented, working system and an easy restart offer, and the moved business gets a fresh quote at its new site. What a save never does is bury a term extension in a discount, retention-by-obstruction, or promise fixes the operations bench cannot deliver; a save bought with a lie churns again with interest.

included: plain-terms discount, downsize or pause moves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: re-churn of saved accounts, discount-frequency drift, or winback conversion evidence

pros.claim: Root-cause saves retain the account and delete the failure class that endangered it
pros.example: saving a gym by fixing the gap-alerting that missed its lobby camera, a fix every other site inherited the same month

cons.claim: Save discounts leak margin and teach customers that threatening cancellation is the price menu
cons.example: a plaza's three tenants comparing notes and each calling to cancel every renewal season for the ritual discount

failure_modes: discounting to mask an operational failure that then recurs and churns the account anyway
smuggling a term extension into a save and converting a wobble into a betrayal
acceptance_tests: each save on record ties to the account's root cause with the corrective action taken, its terms stated plainly with no undisclosed commitment change, and structural exits show the winback seed planted
revisit_triggers: saved accounts re-churning within a review period
save-discount frequency rising across the book

nodes.definition: Execute cancellations so cleanly that the last impression matches the first: confirm the effective date in writing, offer a final export of footage the owner wants kept (delivered with the same integrity discipline as any evidence export), then on the date revoke every viewer account, close the operator's own access, delete the cloud-held footage and account data per the retention policy's disposition rules, and hand the customer a dated record of what was deleted and when. Hardware questions are settled by the contract the offer practice wrote - customer-owned cameras keep working locally or with another service, and the operator says so honestly instead of implying the gear dies without them. A well-run offboarding costs an hour and buys years of reputation; a vindictive or sloppy one - orphaned access, lingering footage, dark hints about the equipment - is the story that circulates at the chamber mixer.

included: final export offer and confirmed dates
documented deletion and honest hardware disposition
excluded: save attempts before the decision is final

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a residual-access or residual-data finding on a closed account, or a disposition-record dispute

pros.claim: A documented deletion record closes the operator's custodial liability the day the relationship ends
pros.example: an ex-customer's later data-protection inquiry answered with the dated disposition certificate instead of a scramble through old cloud consoles

cons.claim: Meticulous offboarding spends real hours on accounts that will never pay again
cons.example: a technician's afternoon revoking accounts and certifying deletion for a site lost to a national discounter

failure_modes: leaving the operator's own admin access alive on a cancelled site - a breach waiting to be attributed
footage surviving past the promised deletion because nobody verified the purge
acceptance_tests: every completed cancellation shows the export offer made, all access revoked both directions on the effective date, deletion verified and certified in writing, and the hardware disposition stated honestly
revisit_triggers: an ex-customer inquiry about retained data
an audit finds residual access or footage on any closed account

nodes.definition: Close the loop on everything above with a recurring operations review: postmortem every failed or late retrieval, every incident a camera missed, every audit anomaly and every churn event; retune what the evidence indicts - alert thresholds drowning signal, ladder steps that never work, report formats nobody reads, register verify-dates gone stale; and route the findings that are not operations' to fix across the practice boundaries - chronic coverage complaints and hardware failure patterns to the design-and-installation practice, tier-economics evidence and competitive-loss patterns to the offer practice - through a documented handoff rather than hallway grumbling. The review also samples healthy sites, not just failures, so drift is caught before it fails: a spot-check that signage photos are current, purges executing, access recertifications on schedule. This node is why year three of the book runs better than year one instead of accumulating scar tissue.

excluded: executing offer or design changes in the other practices

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recurrence of a postmortemed failure class or feedback that handoff findings failed to land

pros.claim: Postmortems convert each painful failure into a permanent deletion of its failure class
pros.example: one missed break-in on a gapped camera producing the coverage-check rule that then caught nine silent failures across the book

cons.claim: Review cadences decay under daily firefighting precisely when they are most needed
cons.example: the quarter with the worst alert flood being the quarter the review that would have fixed it got skipped

failure_modes: reviews that catalog failures without changing a single threshold, runbook line or report format
fixing symptoms locally while the systemic cause belongs to design or offer and never gets handed off
acceptance_tests: the latest review shows each qualifying failure postmortemed with an action, at least one healthy-site drift sample, and cross-practice findings delivered through the documented handoff
revisit_triggers: a failure class recurs after its postmortem action
either sibling practice reports the handoff findings are not actionable

edges.why_related: the lawful-use rule enforces the charter's stated purpose of disclosed owner surveillance
the register operationalizes the compliance duties the charter obligates per site
retention windows are chosen inside the obligation classes the register names
signage wording and audio posture implement the site's registered consent and notice classes
the charter's viewer-administration obligation is delivered by the access model
the audit trail logs the named, scoped accounts the access model creates
health monitoring delivers the charter's core promise that footage will exist when needed
triage consumes the severity-routed alerts monitoring produces
the retention window is the largest consumption driver storage reconciliation must respect
health telemetry supplies the per-camera recording and settings data reconciliation reads
firmware state is a monitored health signal and patch waves are watched through the same telemetry
retrieval can only serve requests that fall inside the retention windows the engine enforces
the retrieval authority check resolves requesters against the access model's roles
third-party adjudication extends the retrieval pipeline with the non-owner authority rules
which instruments compel production and which data-subject rights exist come from the register's classes
evidence-grade export and hold placement are invoked from within the retrieval pipeline
tier operation delivers the per-tier obligations the charter maps
uptime, health events and fixes are the report's primary content
unread or unpersuasive reports and reported failures are churn signals the map consumes
right-sizing at renewal works against the tier definitions and delivery records tier operation keeps
a save is constructed from the account's root cause recorded in the churn map
offboarding executes the unobstructed cancellation the renewal practice honors
the review reconciles reported service against underlying records and mines both for retuning
purpose limitation caps what any role may be scoped to view, including the operator's own staff
retrieval serves the owner's lawful deterrence-detection-evidence purposes and refuses personal-surveillance fishing
the tier's response class bounds the fix expectations triage may promise a site
offboarding deletion follows the disposition rules the retention policy defines
undetected camera death discovered at incident time is the strongest ops-removable churn driver, so health coverage directly moves churn
successful retrievals are the most persuasive value evidence the report carries
a year of honest delivered-value reports is what lets a plain renewal close without pressure
a hijacked or leaking camera fleet destroys the trust the subscription rests on and churns the book beyond the breached site
when the save fails or the driver is structural, the account proceeds to clean offboarding
every disclosure decision is written into the audit trail after adjudication so the owner can see who received footage
postmortem evidence retunes severity classes, ladder steps and thresholds
churn root causes tied to tier mismatch reshape plan-fit conversations and the cost-to-serve evidence sent to the offer practice
audit anomalies drive role tightening, revocations and recertification of stale accounts
both are demonstrable-compliance artifacts: one proves people were told about recording, the other proves who watched it
longer retention comforts the customer and raises evidence odds while directly inflating the cloud bill the plan must carry
edges.resolution_rule: the contracted retention window wins over storage-cost pressure; cost is managed through settings that do not touch the promise, and a window that is truly uneconomic is repriced or renegotiated openly at plan-fit or renewal, never shortened silently

edges.why_related: the retrieval pipeline optimizes for fast helpful delivery while third-party adjudication imposes verification friction on exactly the most urgent-feeling requests
edges.resolution_rule: authority verification wins over speed for any non-owner requester: release happens only with owner authorization or a compelling instrument of the registered class, urgency escalates the verification effort rather than waiving it, and the verify-locally flag governs contested cases

edges.why_related: retention pressure tempts save offers toward hidden term extensions and obstruction that the renewal code prohibits
edges.resolution_rule: the honesty code wins: a save may fix, discount, downsize or pause on plainly stated terms, but any move that hides a commitment change or obstructs exit is out of bounds regardless of the revenue at stake

conflict_axes.name: retention_length_vs_privacy_minimization
conflict_axes.description: Longer retention raises the odds late-discovered incidents still have footage, while privacy obligation classes and data-minimization principles push windows shorter.
poles: keep footage longer for evidence value
delete sooner to honor privacy minimization
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the window per camera group from stated evidence need bounded by the register's obligation classes, document the reasoning, and revisit on incident or register change rather than defaulting long

conflict_axes.name: retrieval_speed_vs_disclosure_verification
conflict_axes.description: The service's value moment is fast footage delivery, but the most urgent-sounding requests are exactly where releasing to the wrong party does irreversible harm.
poles: deliver footage as fast as possible
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pre-verify the owner's designated requesters so owner requests are instantly fast, and route every non-owner request through the adjudication rule where urgency escalates effort, never waives it

conflict_axes.name: alert_sensitivity_vs_noise_fatigue
conflict_axes.description: Sensitive health thresholds catch degradation early but flood triage with noise that trains the bench to ignore alerts, burying the one that matters.
poles: alert only on confirmed sustained failures
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tier thresholds by camera criticality, deduplicate flapping sources, and let the ops review retune on evidence of buried or missed alerts

conflict_axes.name: remote_fix_economics_vs_onsite_certainty
conflict_axes.description: Remote fixes protect subscription margin but can retry hopeless cases for days, while truck rolls resolve decisively at the cost that erodes the account's economics.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cap remote attempts by severity class, dispatch immediately on physical-damage indicators, and batch visits with due site checks to amortize the roll

conflict_axes.name: storage_cost_control_vs_promised_quality
conflict_axes.description: Bitrate, resolution and recording-mode tuning shrink the cloud bill but can quietly degrade the footage below evidentiary usefulness the customer paid for.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: tune only within quality floors verified against the site's evidence purposes (readable plates, identifiable faces at doors), and take genuine over-consumption to a plan-fit conversation instead of quality cuts

conflict_axes.name: owner_convenience_vs_least_privilege
conflict_axes.description: Owners want frictionless shared access for whoever is on shift, while least-privilege discipline demands named scoped accounts that feel slower day to day.
poles: easy shared access for the site's staff
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: make the compliant path convenient - fast named-account provisioning, role templates per site type - and explain that attributability protects the owner's own staff from suspicion

conflict_axes.name: save_the_account_vs_honest_exit
conflict_axes.description: Every cancellation signal tempts retention-at-any-cost moves, while the business's referral reputation depends on exits being easy and honest.
poles: let go cleanly when the customer decides
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: save through root-cause fixes and plainly stated commercial moves while the customer is deciding; the moment the decision is final, switch to exemplary offboarding

conflict_axes.name: patch_urgency_vs_recording_continuity
conflict_axes.description: Prompt patching closes vulnerability windows but risks bricking cameras or interrupting recording, while cautious delay leaves the fleet exposed.
poles: defer patches to protect recording continuity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stage every rollout through a pilot group in maintenance windows; escalate to fleet-urgent only for actively exploited remote vulnerability classes, accepting the continuity risk knowingly

conflict_axes.name: report_transparency_vs_self_protection
conflict_axes.description: Honest reports that admit outages and misses build renewal credibility but hand the customer ammunition, while sanitized reports feel safer and rot trust when reality leaks.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always report the failure with cause and corrective action; a customer who learns of a hidden outage independently churns harder than one told promptly

conflict_axes.name: public_safety_cooperation_vs_owner_control
conflict_axes.description: Helping law enforcement canvassing feels civic and builds goodwill, but the footage belongs to the owner and disclosure without authority betrays the custodial duty.
poles: release only with owner authorization or compulsion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: brief owners at onboarding on how requests will be handled, make reaching them for authorization fast, and honor compelling instruments of the registered class - sympathy is never an authority

edge_cases.description: A customer asks mid-contract to aim an existing camera into the neighboring lot or to add a concealed camera in a staff break area
edge_cases.trigger: an in-flight service request crosses the lawful-disclosed boundary
edge_cases.mitigation: decline in writing with the reason and the jurisdictional flag, offer the lawful alternative (repositioned disclosed coverage of the owner's own space), and log the request and refusal

edge_cases.description: An incident is discovered after the retention window already purged the relevant footage
edge_cases.trigger: a retrieval request arrives for a time band outside the site's window
edge_cases.mitigation: explain honestly that deletion executed exactly as contracted, show the documented window, and run the retention review to decide with the owner whether the window should change going forward

edge_cases.description: A police officer phones asking for portal access or footage without the owner being reachable
edge_cases.trigger: a law-enforcement request lacking owner authorization or a produced instrument
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the requester's identity, pursue the owner's authorization urgently, release only on that authorization or a compelling instrument of the registered class, and log the decision either way with the verify-locally flag consulted

edge_cases.description: A terminated manager still opens the viewer app weeks after leaving the customer's employ
edge_cases.trigger: the customer never reported the departure and no revocation event fired
edge_cases.mitigation: revoke on discovery, review the audit trail for the orphan account's activity and disclose findings to the owner, and add departure-reporting to onboarding and recertification prompts

edge_cases.description: A camera stopped writing footage weeks ago while still streaming live, discovered only when its footage is needed
edge_cases.trigger: a retrieval fails on a recording gap monitoring never caught
edge_cases.mitigation: postmortem why the gap check missed it, extend coverage verification to the failure class, and treat the account as churn-critical with an honest account of the miss and the fix

edge_cases.description: A vendor firmware wave bricks one camera model across multiple sites overnight
edge_cases.trigger: a fleet-wide push skipped or outran the pilot stage
edge_cases.mitigation: halt the wave, roll back or replace per the vendor's recovery path, notify affected sites with recording-gap honesty, and re-enforce the pilot-first rule in the runbook

edge_cases.description: A site's upload bandwidth degrades and cloud copies silently gap during business hours while cameras look healthy
edge_cases.trigger: ISP throttling or a new bandwidth consumer on the customer's network
edge_cases.mitigation: distinguish connectivity-caused gaps from camera faults in monitoring, apply the recording-mode and local-buffer mechanisms the platform offers, and route persistent undersupply to a design-practice handoff

edge_cases.description: An employee of the customer requests footage of themselves, invoking a data-subject-style access right
edge_cases.trigger: a jurisdiction whose data-protection class treats footage as the recorded person's personal data
edge_cases.mitigation: log the request, consult the site's registered class with the verify-locally flag, coordinate the owner's response within the class's expectations, and refer contested cases to counsel rather than adjudicating law

edge_cases.description: A preservation letter arrives the same day auto-purge would delete the footage it names
edge_cases.trigger: legal-hold notice racing the purge schedule
edge_cases.mitigation: place the scoped hold immediately on intake ahead of any review, verify purge suspension took effect, and date-stamp both so the response is provable

edge_cases.description: The customer's business is sold and the new owner expects to inherit the subscription, the accounts and the historical footage
edge_cases.trigger: ownership change on an active site
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as offboard-plus-onboard: contract assignment or new agreement, full access reset, prior-era footage disposition decided with the departing owner whose data it is, and a fresh register review for the new operation

edge_cases.description: At renewal the owner says nothing ever happened all year, so the subscription seems pointless
edge_cases.trigger: an incident-free year reads as value-free to the customer
edge_cases.mitigation: walk the year's reports - camera failures caught and fixed, coverage verified, deterrence context - and offer right-sizing honestly if the usage truly says a lower tier fits

edge_cases.description: One viewer account repeatedly exports footage of a staff-only area with no incident tickets behind it
edge_cases.trigger: audit review surfaces a viewing pattern consistent with monitoring a person rather than protecting property
edge_cases.mitigation: escalate the pattern to the site owner as their duty to manage, restrict the role pending their response, and document the escalation - the operator does not host personal surveillance

workflow.description: Convert the sold offer into the per-site operations contract with tier, retention window, reporting cadence and not-included list
workflow.gate: every active site has a charter the crew operates from, including the explicit not-included list

workflow.action: Build and date the privacy obligation register
workflow.description: Name each site's video, audio-consent, notice and data-protection obligation classes with the operated response and verify-locally flag
workflow.gate: each site lists its classes, responses and a last-verified date inside the review cadence

workflow.action: Set retention and signage into live operation
workflow.description: Choose per-camera-group windows from evidence need and obligation classes, wire purge automation to them, and confirm signage and audio posture match the register
workflow.artifact: retention schedule with purge configuration and signage photo set
workflow.gate: configured retention equals the contracted window per group and the signage-and-posture check is evidenced

workflow.action: Provision least-privilege access and audit logging
workflow.description: Create named scoped MFA accounts, reserve export rights, bound operator support access, and switch on view/export logging
workflow.artifact: role matrix with active audit trail
workflow.gate: no shared logins exist, support access is ticket-bound, and the trail captures view and export events

workflow.action: Stand up fleet health monitoring and triage
workflow.description: Enable offline, recording-gap, image-quality, storage and clock monitoring with severity routing into the triage runbook
workflow.artifact: health dashboard with alert rules and triage runbook
workflow.gate: every camera reports health on cadence and recording-gap checks run against expected coverage

workflow.description: Compare per-site consumption against plan assumptions, name drift causes, and resolve by retune or plan-fit conversation
workflow.gate: material drift shows a named cause and a resolution that never silently cuts promised retention or quality

workflow.action: Operate the retrieval and disclosure pipeline
workflow.description: Run intake, authority check, indexed search, clip assembly and logged delivery, with third-party adjudication and hold or evidence-export handling where invoked
workflow.artifact: retrieval runbook with request and disclosure log
workflow.gate: every export ties to a verified authorized requester and is logged with recipient and purpose

workflow.action: Maintain firmware, credential and isolation hygiene
workflow.description: Watch advisories for deployed models, run staged patch waves, keep credentials and certificates clean, spot-check isolation on visits
workflow.artifact: patch and vulnerability log with visit spot-check records
workflow.gate: patch state is within cadence or dated-excepted, and no default credentials exist in the fleet

workflow.description: Report uptime, fixes, retrievals, retention status and access changes per tier cadence, including failures with corrective actions
workflow.gate: the report reconciles with health and retrieval records and includes every qualifying failure honestly

workflow.action: Run the renewal, save and offboarding cycle
workflow.description: Send plain advance notice, right-size on actual usage, construct root-cause saves for wobbling accounts, and execute clean offboarding with deletion evidence for exits
workflow.artifact: renewal records, save log and offboarding certificates
workflow.gate: renewals show dated notice and disclosed changes, saves show plainly stated terms, and exits show export offer, revocation and certified deletion

workflow.action: Review, retune and hand findings across practices
workflow.description: Postmortem failures, sample healthy sites for drift, retune alerting and reporting, and route design- and offer-owned findings through the documented handoff
workflow.artifact: quarterly ops review with churn analysis and handoff notes
workflow.gate: each qualifying failure shows a postmortem action and cross-practice findings show a delivered handoff

priority_rationale: The frame nodes - the service charter, the lawful-use boundary and the privacy register - come first because every operational setting downstream is either an obligation they define or a boundary they enforce; retention, signage, access and audit make the compliance posture real before volume operations begin; health monitoring, triage, storage reconciliation and firmware hygiene keep the recording promise true day to day; the footage pipeline turns that promise into delivered evidence under authority control; and the subscription layer - tiers, reporting, churn, renewals, saves and offboarding - converts honestly delivered service into durable recurring revenue, with the ops review feeding every lesson back.

dominance_rules.rule: Lawful, disclosed operation dominates any customer request or revenue consideration
dominance_rules.rationale: one accommodated covert request converts the operator from service provider to accomplice and poisons the whole book
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for covert coverage, out-of-right aiming, undisclosed audio or personal-surveillance use
dominance_rules.action: decline in writing with the reason and a lawful alternative, and log the refusal

dominance_rules.rule: The site's registered obligation classes dominate operational convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: privacy, consent and signage duties are jurisdictional facts the operator cannot tune away
dominance_rules.trigger: any retention, audio, signage or disclosure setting that would conflict with a registered class
dominance_rules.action: conform the setting to the register and verify current local rules before changing either

dominance_rules.rule: The contracted retention window dominates storage-cost pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: silently shortening a promised window is a broken promise discovered at the worst possible moment
dominance_rules.trigger: cloud-bill pressure or consumption drift tempting a quiet window cut
dominance_rules.action: manage cost through non-promise settings or an open plan-fit or repricing conversation, never a silent reduction

dominance_rules.rule: Authority verification dominates disclosure speed for any non-owner request
dominance_rules.rationale: a wrongly released clip is irreversible harm to the owner and the people recorded
dominance_rules.trigger: a third-party footage request of any urgency
dominance_rules.action: require verified identity plus owner authorization or a compelling instrument of the registered class before release, and log the decision

dominance_rules.rule: An active legal hold dominates auto-purge
dominance_rules.rationale: deleting preserved-notice footage on schedule converts routine automation into spoliation exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: a preservation letter, litigation notice or investigation touching identified footage
dominance_rules.action: place the scoped hold immediately on intake and verify purge suspension before anything else

dominance_rules.rule: Least-privilege and audit discipline dominate owner convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: shared logins make every misuse unattributable and every departure a standing breach
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for shared credentials or unscoped all-camera access
dominance_rules.action: provision named scoped accounts instead and make the compliant path fast enough to remove the complaint

dominance_rules.rule: The honest-renewal code dominates save-the-account pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: a save bought with hidden terms churns worse later and spends the referral reputation the pipeline runs on
dominance_rules.trigger: a retention move that would hide a term change or obstruct cancellation
dominance_rules.action: limit saves to root-cause fixes and plainly stated commercial moves, and let the account go cleanly if they fail

dominance_rules.rule: For actively exploited vulnerability classes, patching dominates recording continuity; otherwise staged maintenance dominates patch urgency
dominance_rules.rationale: a hijacked fleet is a worse outcome than a maintenance window, but routine patches never justify fleet-wide recording risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a vulnerability disclosure affecting deployed camera or recorder models
dominance_rules.action: classify the exposure; run fleet-urgent isolation and patching for exploited remote classes, and pilot-staged windows for everything else

dominance_rules.rule: Root-cause correction dominates discounting when saving an at-risk account
dominance_rules.rationale: a discount on an unfixed operational failure rents the account until the failure recurs
dominance_rules.trigger: a save opportunity whose churn driver is ops-removable
dominance_rules.action: fix the cause and show what changed; apply commercial moves only on top of, never instead of, the fix

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the site's privacy obligation register before configuring retention, audio or signage
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconfiguring schedules and reposting signage after an obligation class surfaces late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enable recording-gap and coverage verification before the first retrieval promise is relied on
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering silently dead cameras at incident time and rebuilding trust account by account

anti_rework_rules.rule: Provision named scoped accounts with audit logging at handover, not after the first misuse complaint
anti_rework_rules.prevents: untangling who saw what from a shared-login era with no attributable history

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the per-group retention window into the contract before wiring purge automation to it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: purge deleting footage the customer believed was promised longer, and the dispute that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify requester authority before any export leaves, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unrecallable disclosure and the incident response that dwarfs the minutes verification costs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stage every firmware wave through a pilot group before the fleet
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a book-wide bricked-camera weekend from a single bad vendor release

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile storage consumption before renewal and repricing conversations
anti_rework_rules.prevents: renewal-table surprises and back-billing arguments built on a year of unexamined drift

anti_rework_rules.rule: Root-cause a churn signal before constructing its save offer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discount-only saves that leave the operational cause alive to churn the account again

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the export offer, revocations and deletion evidence at the moment of offboarding
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing disposition months later for an ex-customer inquiry with the accounts already gone

iteration_protocol.trigger: a jurisdictional rule change, counsel input or industry alert touches a registered obligation class
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the register entries, re-verify locally, and reconcile retention, signage and audio settings at every affected site

iteration_protocol.trigger: a retrieval fails, misses its response class, or exposes a gap monitoring never caught
iteration_protocol.action: postmortem the failure, extend gap detection or the runbook to the failure class, and address the account honestly

iteration_protocol.trigger: the audit review surfaces an unexplained viewing or export pattern
iteration_protocol.action: restrict the implicated role, escalate to the site owner or operator management, and tighten the access model per the finding

iteration_protocol.trigger: alert-noise review shows real failures buried or thresholds flapping
iteration_protocol.action: retune severity classes and thresholds, deduplicate noisy sources, and re-verify detection of the critical failure classes

iteration_protocol.trigger: storage reconciliation shows consumption drifting beyond plan assumptions across sites
iteration_protocol.action: name the driver per site, retune within quality floors, and queue plan-fit conversations where usage genuinely outgrew the plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: churn events cluster or the ops-removable share of the driver mix rises
iteration_protocol.action: re-root-cause the cluster, fix the indicted operational class, and hand structural-market findings to the offer practice

iteration_protocol.trigger: a vulnerability disclosure lands for camera or recorder models deployed in the book
iteration_protocol.action: classify the exposure, run the staged or fleet-urgent patch path, verify isolation, and notify affected customers honestly
